PullRequest.Title: Finalize timeline API and remove proposal checks

Scenarios.Scenario: Git extension activation and file/workspace timeline provider registration after repository discovery
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The providers become visible only after the extension-host registration messages are processed on the main thread. The diff still performs the same file-provider and workspace-provider registrations; it only moves id/label from provider properties to explicit arguments and removes a constant-time proposal check.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Register the file/folder timeline provider in MainThreadTimeline and TimelineService.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same IPC registration occurred with id and label read from the provider object.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before the source is available to the Timeline view; not awaited by extension initialization.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Register the workspace timeline provider in MainThreadTimeline and TimelineService.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same IPC registration occurred with id and label read from the provider object.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before the workspace source is available; not awaited by extension initialization.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One paired registration per GitTimelineProvider lifetime; repository count does not multiply registration because ensureProviderRegistration is guarded by providerDisposable.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Two fire-and-forget registration IPC messages are issued back-to-back once. Repeated repository-open events are coalesced by the existing registration guard.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No result cache is involved. Provider maps and event subscriptions have the same insertion and disposal lifetime before and after the diff.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed call sites and both registration implementations show identical map/listener/IPC work aside from argument sourcing and removal of proposal lookup.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact IPC latency varies by extension-host placement, but the diff does not increase call count, payload scale, or waiting.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: registration frequency, lifecycle, IPC cardinality, and downstream work are unchanged, while one small proposal-array lookup is removed.

Scenarios.Scenario: Opening, refreshing, or paging a file/folder Timeline backed by the Git provider
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The Timeline pane issues one request per included visible source; MainThreadTimeline forwards one RPC to the extension host, then Git performs its existing stat/history/detail work before items render. None of this request scheduling or provider implementation is changed by the diff.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request and return one timeline page between main thread and extension host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One round trip per included source per cold load, refresh, or necessary page.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same provider RPC was issued using the same registered source id.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The returned page is on the render critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Determine whether the target URI is a folder with workspace.fs.stat.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One stat per Git file/folder timeline request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same stat was already performed by the unchanged provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Completes before history query options can be selected.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read Git file history and supporting commit/tree/detail data.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One page-oriented logFile call plus the existing fixed/detail operations for the returned page.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The identical Git provider method and operations were invoked before the API signature change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Git history and details must complete before the page is returned.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective cardinality is the number of non-excluded timeline sources, with one request per source and a page-sized commit set per Git request; load-more uses the provider cursor.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Sources are started without awaiting one another. There is at most one current pending request per source; replacement cancels the previous token. Git's file request performs its existing operations mostly sequentially.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The pane avoids querying completed timelines, uses cursors for paging, and asks the extension host to cache item objects. Reset clears the single-URI item/command cache. Cold and warm behavior are unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the pane, main-thread bridge, cache, and Git provider call path were traced, and the changed lines only alter registration metadata plumbing.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Repository size, remote filesystem latency, and extension-contributed detail providers affect duration, but none of those dimensions is changed by this PR.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: no boundary is added or moved, and request count, cancellation, paging, cache behavior, and expensive Git work remain identical.

Scenarios.Scenario: Opening, refreshing, or paging the workspace Timeline across multiple repositories
Scenarios.CriticalPath: One source RPC reaches provideWorkspaceTimeline, which launches the existing per-repository Git log work and then resolves details only for repositories contributing to the selected page. Results are required before rendering.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request and return the workspace timeline page between main thread and extension host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One round trip for the Git source per cold load, refresh, or required page.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same workspace provider RPC occurred under the same id.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The workspace page waits for the provider response.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run repository history queries and supporting detail/tree queries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One concurrent log per effective repository, then existing detail operations only for repositories represented in the page.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same Promise.all fan-out and page grouping existed before the registration signature change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All log promises and represented-repository details complete before page return.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: R repositories after cursor filtering; one log per effective repository, followed by detail work for the distinct repositories represented in the page and at most the requested page size of items.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The existing Promise.all starts repository logs concurrently with no new limiter; detail preparation is also concurrent across contributing repositories. The diff neither increases R nor changes this scheduling.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The cursor records per-root skips, the pane caches loaded aggregate items, and the extension host caches command item objects until reset/disposal. Cold/warm and invalidation behavior are unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: provider registration still reaches the same implementation, and the unchanged workspace method establishes exact grouping and concurrency.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large multi-root/worktree counts can make the pre-existing burst costly, but this PR does not alter effective repository cardinality or concurrency.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the potentially expensive multi-repository fan-out is pre-existing and is neither introduced nor materially amplified by the diff.

Scenarios.Scenario: Invoking a Timeline item context command, including GitHub's Open on GitHub action and multi-selection arguments
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The action crosses the contributed-command IPC boundary, then the extension host resolves cached action contexts to original items for the owner or readonly copies for another extension before running the command. GitHub then performs its existing branch lookup and opens the selected URL.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch a contributed Timeline command from the workbench to the target extension host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One dispatch per user command invocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same command dispatch occurred; proposal-enabled consumers such as the built-in GitHub extension passed the removed gate.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Argument resolution and command completion are on the user-invoked action path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Query remote branches containing the selected commit.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One Git API branch query per Open on GitHub invocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: GitHub declared the timeline proposal, so this exact command and branch query already ran before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before selecting a matching GitHub remote and opening the URL.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open the generated GitHub commit URL externally.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one openExternal call per successful invocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same external-open call occurred for proposal-enabled Timeline action arguments.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Occurs after branch resolution; it is the terminal user action.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One primary item plus selected items from the same provider; readonly-copy CPU/allocation grows linearly with selected item count and trusted-command metadata size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Argument processing is synchronous and serial for command arguments and selected items. The downstream GitHub command performs one branch query for the chosen commit.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Original items are looked up in the existing provider/URI map. Readonly copies are not cached. For GitHub, pre-diff proposal enablement meant the same copies were already produced; provider cache reset/disposal is unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the call path and linear copy behavior; lower only for ecosystem prevalence and selection sizes, which is why no speculative finding is submitted.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Third-party adoption of the newly stable API and unusually large selections are unknown. The newly reachable readonly-copy allocation is user-invoked and required by the documented isolation semantics, with no evidence of a realistic latency or memory regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: built-in behavior and expensive boundaries are unchanged. Removing the proposal gate intentionally exposes the finalized API; the only newly reachable work is per-invocation argument materialization needed for the public command contract, without a concrete harmful trigger.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 13 changed files and all diff pages. Traced provider registration, file and workspace timeline loading, caching/cancellation/lifecycle, command argument copying, and Git/GitHub filesystem, subprocess, IPC, and external-open boundaries. The PR changes API gating and metadata plumbing but does not add or amplify a concrete expensive mechanism; no findings were submitted.
